title: Full-Motion mobile reflector antenna (IoSiS-NG Project)
description: In the context of the IoSiS-NG project, the procurement of a mobile X-band radar receive antenna, equipped with a full-motion two-axis positioner for the purpose of object tracking in low earth orbit (LEO), inclusive of the antenna control unit, has been planned. The antenna pedestal shall be mounted on a mobile platform (e.g., car trailer), enabling the repositioning the antenna. German road approval of trailer required. The antenna control unit must support an Ethernet interface, allowing for TLE orbit tracking and live tracking data input. An alignment system (RF or optical) must be provided for a pointing accuracy sufficient for tracking (no auto-tracking) of objects in LEO. The repositioning and realignment of the antenna must be possible within one working day (i.e.,8 h). The antennas shall have a reflector diameter of 2 to 3 meters. The antenna will be located on the DLR site in Weilheim (Germany). The antenna positioning velocities must be fast enough to track objects in LEO with a keyhole of less than 5°. All mechanical accuracies of the antennas must be sufficient to operate them in X-band (up to 12.4 GHz). The antenna feed horn is planned to be developed by the buyer. But a X band feed horn can optionally be provided by the antenna supplier (8-12,4 GHz, linear polarized, receive only). The RF electronics will be developed and integrated by the customer. All technical specifications of the antenna must be provided. This includes but may not be limited to all technical drawings with dimensions, CAD models, … A final check of the agreed-upon technical requirements is carried out on-site at DLR Weilheim jointly by DLR and the supplier. A weatherproof housing on the mobile platform (Two separated racks with approx. 19” 20U) has to be provided by the antenna supplier, suitable for housing electronic and RF components. No ITAR devices The following must also be observed: The requirements of the export control law applicable to the project must be taken into account, in particular the handling of goods under the Foreign Trade and Payments Ordinance (AWV), the EC Dual-Use Regulation (EC Regulation 428/2009), the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR).

title: France – Geological, geophysical and other scientific prospecting services – Marine survey by unmanned or autonomous vehicles
description: RTE, the French electricity transmission system operator, is responsible for developing, building and operating high-voltage submarine links for interconnection with neighbouring countries, or for connecting offshore wind farms to the terrestrial transmission grid. RTE currently operates a wide range of submarine cables on the Manche Channel, Atlantic and Mediterranean facades. In the future, the number of cables shall further increase with the development of HVDC long distance links to offshore wind farms. These cables can be floating or laid on the sea floor. In this context, RTE carries out regular submarine data collection campaigns during the design, construction, and operational maintenance phases of its assets. These campaigns may include bathymetric surveys, geophysical soundings, UXO findings, optical monitoring of structures or environmental monitoring and measurements. Currently carried out by conventional means (surface vessels or on foot at landfall), these investigations could in the future be carried out by autonomous or remotely-controlled robots/vehicles. In addition to reducing costs, the expected benefits include operational efficiency, reduced risk for personnel, and a smaller environmental footprint for operations, as well as the accuracy of the data collected. RTE would like to investigate on innovative autonomous or remote solutions applicable to its scope of service for cables, particularly AUVs (Autonomous Underwater Vehicles), USVs (Unmanned Surface Sehicles) or flying vehicle, which can renew conventional approaches to data acquisition in the marine environment. Hence this inquiry aims to solicit the market to have its various actors emerge and help RTE identify them. It shall also allow the market to clarify its capacity of service with respect to RTE inquiry and propose adapted and robust solutions.
